rationale: The current best already gets real signal from zero-init two-block tail recurrence and from preserving the recurrent final block's QKV under int8 export. This run keeps that path intact and adds the next minimal EvoNAS-style transplant: a zero-init per-channel carry gate that blends each tail block's first-pass output back into its recurrent pass. That gives the shared second traversal an explicit gated state-carryover path, costs only tiny control tensors, adds no shape churn, and should help the repeated tail blocks reuse useful deep features within the 600-second budget without meaningfully increasing artifact size.
title: Gated Tail Carryover On Two-Block Recurrence
